title: Maximum Linear Stock Score
summary: Given an array prices representing stock prices on consecutive days, find the maximum score of a linear selection.
statement: Given an array prices representing stock prices on consecutive days, find the maximum score of a linear selection. A linear selection is a subsequence where the difference between consecutive elements in both the index and price arrays is constant. The score is the sum of the selected prices.
constraints: A valid selection contains indices whose price minus index is the same.
Its score is the sum of selected prices; return the maximum score.
hints: Rearrange the linear condition as price-index = constant.
Accumulate prices by that invariant in a hash map.
For each index and price, add price to totals[price-index]; return the largest total.
Every valid selection lies in exactly one invariant group, and positive prices make taking its whole group optimal.
editorial: Every valid selection lies in exactly one invariant group, and positive prices make taking its whole group optimal.

tests.explanation: Prices at indices 1, 3, and 4 share price-index value four and sum to twenty.
All three entries share price-index value two and total nine.
